title: fix(metadata-admin): definition-list designer items write term/description
body:
Fixes #8279

The page designer's `element:definition-list` item controls were named `label` and `value`. `PageBlockInspector.renderField`'s array branch writes an item key verbatim (`next[i] = { ...itemObj, [n]: v }`), so an author filled `items[i].label` / `items[i].value`. `DefinitionListRenderer` reads `term` and `description`, and its `toText` returns the em-dash for null/undefined/empty.

**Every definition list built in the page designer rendered a blank term and a literal em-dash on every row, whatever the author typed** — and said so nowhere: both authored strings stayed in the document, and `items.length` was non-zero so the renderer's own "No details" empty state never fired either.

Per the PM ruling on the card: the **producer** moves. AGENTS.md #0.1 points there, `block-config.ts`'s own file header states the rule that was broken ("keep each field `name` aligned with the property name the corresponding renderer reads"), and the block's registry declaration already named `items` as "Term/description pairs `[{ term, description }]`" — two of the three faces agreed and the designer was the outlier.

## Clause 2 — this changes what the designer emits

A list authored after this change is written as `items: [{ term, description }]`. Nothing else about the block moved; the renderer is untouched.

## The i18n sites, all moved in the fix commit

The field `name` is the last segment of the i18n key, so 6 sites move together:

| site | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `block-config.ts` itemFields | `name: 'label'` / `name: 'value'` | `name: 'term'` / `name: 'description'` |
| `i18n.ts` en | `…items.label`: `Label`, `…items.value`: `Value` | `…items.term`: `Term`, `…items.description`: `Description` |
| `i18n.ts` zh-CN | `…items.label`: 标签, `…items.value`: 值 | `…items.term`: 术语, `…items.description`: 描述 |
| `i18n.ts` en/zh `…inline` | `Inline (label · value)` / 行内（标签 · 值） | `Inline (term · description)` / 行内（术语 · 描述） |

The retired pair leaves **both** locale tables (objectui#3829 / objectui#5212's pattern). The `inline` label is included because it spelled the retired pair **in its own prose**: leaving it would have put "Inline (label · value)" over two boxes named Term and Description — a fresh mismatch created by this change, in the same panel.

Zero-hit grep for the retired keys across the repo, with an identically-shaped control grep on the new keys that returns all 4 sites (see the report comment on the card for the printed lines).

## The stored-document route: left alone, deliberately

The card and the dispatch both framed this as a strip question. **Measured, the strip is the one route that is affirmatively wrong here**, and the criterion is this repo's own:

- objectui#7772's `RETIRED_BLOCK_PROP_KEYS` admits a key only when **the node schema refuses it by name**, so the strip cannot lose anything a consumer would have honoured.
- `element:definition-list` has **no runtime-judgeable schema on either face** — that is why objectui#8216's parity gate carries it as an explicit exemption (objectui#8281 owns the absence). Nothing refuses these keys.
- The sibling ledger states the consequence outright: *"A key the schema ACCEPTS must never be added here; stripping an accepted key deletes authored metadata."* `items[].label` holds a term a person typed.

A migration (`term ?? label` seeded at the read door, objectui#6526 option B's shape) is the instrument that fits the value — but it is a second de-facto spelling with **no retirement path**: nothing will ever remove the old keys from a stored document, so the alias could never be withdrawn. That is a standing commitment, and it deserves its own card rather than a rider on this one. See the report comment for the full argument and the follow-up.

What an author actually loses is bounded, and measured rather than assumed:

- **Rendering does not regress.** A stored list rendered a blank term and an em-dash before this change and renders identically after it. Pinned.
- The two authored strings stay in the document (pinned: they ride through an unrelated commit rather than being stripped).
- They stay readable and editable in the resource editor's **JSON source tab** — the surface whose own comment names *"nested arrays"* as its reason to exist.
- The author now has a control that works, which they did not have before at any price.

## Verification — this block has no gate, so the measurement is the verification

Two pins, neither with a hand-written item literal between the faces:

- `previews/__tests__/definition-list-item-keys-8279.test.tsx` — assembles an item from `BLOCK_CONFIG`'s own `itemFields` the way the inspector assembles it, renders through the renderer's own registration, reads the DOM.
- `inspectors/PageBlockInspector.definitionListItems-8279.test.tsx` — drives the **real panel** (`fireEvent.change` on the real boxes), reads the committed properties back, and hands those same properties to the real renderer. Inspector out, renderer in.

**Before, on `origin/main`** (run before any edit): the typed text absent from the DOM, and the description cell holding the literal em-dash (`DD.textContent` equal to the em-dash) for a description the author filled in. Three control rows green in the same run, so the red was the keys and not the harness.

**Ablation** (producer item names reverted to `label`/`value`, mutation proven on disk by anchor counts 1→0 / 0→1): 6 rows red **by name** across both pins, 5 rows correctly green. Restored **by state** — `git diff HEAD` empty and `git hash-object` equal to `git rev-parse HEAD:PATH`.

One harness finding worth recording, because it fails silently in the dangerous direction: a recording-only `vi.fn()` for `onPatch` is not sufficient here. Every property write spreads from `blockProps`, which derives from the `draft` prop, so against a host that never re-renders the second field's commit spreads from the stale draft and **drops the first**. Measured on this file's first draft — typing Term then Description committed `{ description }` alone, which reads exactly like the panel overwriting its own items. The host in the committed test applies each patch.

## Gates run locally, with their own verdict lines

| gate | verdict |
|---|---|
| `check:i18n-keys` | exit 0 — "Every in-scope call-site key resolves against the en pack (2976 keys)…" |
| `check:i18n-drift` | exit 0 — "0 en value(s) changed" |
| `check:i18n-dead-keys` | exit 0 — report-only by design, not wired into CI |
| `check:control-bytes` | exit 0 — "OK (scanned 6620 tracked text file(s))" |
| `check:designer-field-key-parity` | exit 0 — "designer-field-key-parity: OK" |
| `check:governed-queue-guard --test` | exit 0 — "NOT GOVERNED — 4 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s)" |
| `check:vi-mock-specifiers` / `check:vi-mock-inherit` | exit 0 |
| `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:changeset-no-major` | exit 0 |
| `check-changeset-presence` | exit 0 — 1 changeset declared |
| `packages/app-shell` `eslint .` | exit 0 — 0 errors (2921 warnings; `--max-warnings` is deliberately unset here) |
| `packages/app-shell` `type-check` | exit 0 (`tsc --noEmit` + `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, so the new tests are compiled) |

Tests, at `0cde2cd0a`, after building the dependency closure (`pnpm --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build`):

- `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/` — **236 files / 2449 passed**, 1 skipped
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/` + the three `views/` files that import the changed i18n table — **56 files / 327 passed**

**Declared narrowing.** The run is scoped to every real consumer of the two changed modules, established by an importer census whose matched lines were printed rather than counted: `block-config.ts` is imported only under `views/metadata-admin/**` and is not re-exported from the package barrel; `metadata-admin/i18n.ts` adds `views/studio-design/**` and three files in `views/`. Two apparent cross-package importers (`packages/test-support`, `packages/i18n/src/__tests__`) turned out to be prose mentions in comments, not imports. The remainder of `packages/app-shell` and the three affected consumers (`apps/console`, two examples) are left to CI. `check:sdui-registration-pins` reads bundle output and needs the console built; it is **not measured** locally rather than reported green — it could not see this change, which adds and removes no registration.

Not done: a browser run. The jsdom round trip already drives the real inspector and the real renderer end to end; a browser would only add the designer canvas wiring, which this change does not touch.
